transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop focusing on my face. There's this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw, and I see it in every single reflection or photo. 

Other people tell me I look fine, but to me, it's just so obvious. It's gotten to the point where it's affecting my work—I've actually started avoiding client meetings and presentations because I can't stand the thought of people looking at it.
When people tell you your face looks fine, is there any part of you that considers they might be right, or do you feel completely certain that what you see is the objective truth?

Honestly... I just think they're being nice. Or maybe they don't want to hurt my feelings. But no, I don't really think they're right. 

When I look in the mirror, the unevenness is just... it's right there. It's so obvious to me. I feel like they just aren't looking closely enough, or they're just used to seeing me. So, yeah, I'm pretty much certain that what I'm seeing is the truth, no matter what anyone else says.

Aside from these concerns about your face, have you noticed anything else unusual lately—like hearing or seeing things others don't, or having thoughts or beliefs that others find strange or hard to believe?

No, nothing like that. I mean... I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, if that's what you're asking. And I don't have any strange beliefs or anything. My mind is perfectly sound, I just... it's really just my face. That's the only thing that's bothering me and taking up all my thoughts.

Do you find yourself doing certain things repeatedly because of how your face looks—like checking mirrors often, trying to cover or fix the area with makeup or your hand, or comparing your face to other people's?

Yes, I do. It actually takes up a lot of my time. Before I go to work, or if there's a family event... I can easily spend hours just checking the bathroom mirror. I'll take pictures on my phone from all different angles to see how the droop looks. Then I end up redoing my makeup over and over, or adjusting my scarf trying to hide it. 

I also find myself asking my husband if my face looks lopsided. And the comparing... yeah, I definitely do that. I'll just sit there and scroll through photos of other women to see how bad my face looks beside theirs. So, yes, I do all of those things.
